builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: GINGER: Spicing Up Graph-Based Vector Search
summary: Ginger replaces existing approximate nearest neighbor search libraries (such as HNSW implementations) with a graph-based index built on PiPNN construction, Nested TurboQuant two-level vector quantization, and AdaptiveGap graph compression. It is an open-source C++ library requiring CPU-based index construction and memory for the compressed graph and quantized vectors; integration effort and build complexity are the main costs, with memory reduced 2.6x versus float32 vectors and graph size reduced up to 2.5x. Adoption can fail if recall targets above 95% are required, if the dataset is small enough that brute force is sufficient, or if integration with existing vector-serving infrastructure adds unacceptable engineering overhead.
rationale: Constrained-infrastructure teams running embedding retrieval in production benefit directly from a faster, smaller, open-source ANNS index that requires no GPU or model training, though recall targets and integration fit should be validated on their own workload.
technique: Graph-based ANNS with two-level vector quantization

claims.statement: Ginger replaces existing approximate nearest neighbor search libraries (such as HNSW implementations) with a graph-based index built on PiPNN construction, Nested TurboQuant two-level vector quantization, and AdaptiveGap graph compression. It is an open-source C++ library requiring CPU-based index construction and memory for the compressed graph and quantized vectors; integration effort and build complexity are the main costs, with memory reduced 2.6x versus float32 vectors and graph size reduced up to 2.5x. Adoption can fail if recall targets above 95% are required, if the dataset is small enough that brute force is sufficient, or if integration with existing vector-serving infrastructure adds unacceptable engineering overhead.

At 95% recall, Ginger speeds up query throughput by an average of 1.8x over each dataset's fastest competitor and by at least 2.3x over any single library, while matching the memory footprint of the most space-efficient competitors.
